No specific error code â€” just a generic installfailed, and it didn't even get far enough to record which version it was trying to install (versionto: null). But when I just ran claude update manually, it succeeded cleanly: "Claude Code is up to date (2.1.220)" â€” no error.

Most likely explanation: the native binary at C:\Users\Fabian\.local\bin\claude.exe can't be overwritten by the auto-updater while a Claude Code session is actively running it (Windows locks executables in use, unlike Linux). The background auto-update probably fired while this session â€” or another terminal running Claude Code â€” had the file open, and the install step failed silently rather than retrying later. The manual check just now likely worked because either the lock was gone, or there simply wasn't a newer version to install.

Nothing appears broken right now â€” you're on the current version and claude doctor otherwise reports no installation issues. If this keeps recurring: close all other running claude sessions/terminals before the next auto-check, or just run claude update manually periodically as a fallback, since that path clearly works.
